title: Proteomic analysis of acid adapted cancer cells
projectDescription: This project uses label-free, quantitative, data-independent acquisition (DIA)- based liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) to reveal the quantitative and qualitative changes in secretion induced by acidic adaptation. Indeed, during acidic adaptation, cancer cells undergo drastic metabolic changes in order to survive, thereby reshaping their tumour niche and affecting neighbouring cells, including non-cancerous counterparts, as well as stromal and immune cells. This analysis focuses on changes in secretion caused by acidic adaptation that could affect neighbouring cells.
sampleProcessingProtocol: The WT MDA-MB-231 cell line and its acid-adapted counterpart (AA MDA-MB- 231, adapted to pH 6.7 for one month) were cultivated to 75% confluence. Once this was reached, the cells were washed with PBS and the regular medium was replaced with a fresh one without FBS or Phenol Red (DMEM, ThermoFisher ref. 31053-028, supplemented with 110 mg/L pyruvate, 580 mg/mL Glutamax and 1% penicillin/streptomycin) with their respective pHs. After 48 hours, the conditioned media were collected, and the cell viability was assessed. Cell debris and large protein aggregates from the conditioned media were removed by two sequential centrifugation steps (first at 300 g for 3 min and second at 2,000 g for 3 min). The proteins in the conditioned media were then concentrated using a Pierce Protein Concentrator at 10,000 g for 10 minutes at 4 °C (Thermofisher, Ref. 88513), after which the protein concentration was determined using BioDrop Duo+ spectrophotometer prior to storage at –70 °C until the samples were further processed. In total three biological replicates per condition and three technical replicates per biological replicate were prepared. For proteomic sample preparation, 50 μg protein from each sample was dried by vacuum centrifugation and resuspended in 10 μL of 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate (ABC). Disulfide bonds were reduced by adding 1 μL of 200 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) to a final concentration of 20 mM and incubating for 30 min at 56 °C, followed by alkylation with 1 μL of 500 mM iodoacetamide (IAA) to a final concentration of 50 mM for 30 min in the dark at room temperature. Excess IAA was quenched by adding 1 μL of 50 mM DTT (to a final concentration of 5 mM) and incubating for 10 min at room temperature. Samples were then diluted with 112 μL of 50 mM ABC to a final volume of 125 μL and digested with 2.5 μg trypsin (1:20 enzyme to protein ratio, w/w) overnight at 37 °C. Digestion was terminated by acidification with 4 μL of 20% trifluoroacetic acid (TFA, v/v), and the final pH was verified to be below 3. A total of 100 ng peptide per sample was desalted and loaded onto Evotip C18 columns following the manufacturer’s protocol and stored in 0.1% formic acid (v/v) at 4 OC until LC-MS/MS analysis. Liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) was performed in data-independent acquisition (DIA) mode on a Thermo Scientific Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometer coupled to an Evosep One LC system set to a standard setup (30 SPD) with a total runtime of 44 min. Peptides were separated on an Evosep Endurance column (15 cm × 150 μm ID, 1.9 μm beads) with a 500 nL/min gradient flow. Peptide samples were ionized via a nanospray ionization (NSI) source at +1.8 kV and transferred through a heated ion transfer tube maintained at 280 °C. Full MS scans were acquired in the Orbitrap at 240,000 resolution (at 200 m/z) over an m/z range of 400–1000 using a normalized AGC target of 300% (absolute value of 3 × 10⁶) and 5 ms maximum injection time. DIA MS/MS scans were collected across the 400–1000 m/z range using 2 m/z isolation windows (300 scan events total, 0.6 s cycle time) with a normalized collision energy of 30% (HCD) and Astral detector for high-speed fragment ion detection. Fragment ions were recorded at 140–2000 m/z in centroid mode with 3.5 ms maximum injection time. All data were acquired in positive polarity with advanced peak determination enabled and an expected LC peak width of 15 s.
dataProcessingProtocol: Thermo .raw files were processed using Spectronaut v19.9 in directDIATM mode (default settings) using Homo sapiens UniProt reference proteome (2024-12 release, 20,644 entries). Trypsin/P was set as the digestion enzyme with up to two missed cleavages allowed. Carbamidomethylation of cysteine (C) was specified as a fixed modification, while oxidation of methionine (M) and protein N-terminal acetylation were set as variable modifications. The minimum and maximum peptide lengths were set to 7 and 52, respectively. Peptide-spectrum matches (PSM), peptides and protein groups were filtered at 1% FDR.
